issues.description: Class name mismatch: the problem statement and template refer to concrete classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g., UML entries and task descriptions). The solution repository does not provide implementations for Seal, Pig, or Goat (Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java are empty); instead it provides implementations named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This difference between expected class identifiers (Seal, Pig, Goat) and the solution identifiers (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat) will confuse students and/or automated graders that expect the canonical class names from the specification and may cause tests or examples (e.g., Main.java) to fail or be misleading.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifiers consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Add concrete implementations Seal, Pig, and Goat in the solution repository (each extending Animal and implementing the same interfaces and behavior as the provided SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat), remove or keep Space* classes as aliases, and update any references so tests and examples use Seal/Pig/Goat; or (B) Update the problem statement, template (including Main.java and UML), and tests to refer to SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead of Seal/Pig/Goat. Prefer option A to match the exercise text and avoid renaming in the specification.

issues.description: The exercise describes and the template code refers to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (problem statement and template Main instantiate Seal, Pig, Goat), but the solution repository implements these entities with different identifiers: SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. Concept: the concrete animal classes expected by the exercise. Problem statement and template: refer to Seal, Pig, Goat. Solution repository: provides SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat. This mismatch prevents a direct mapping between the requirement (and the template's example usage) and the solution code; students looking for Seal, Pig, Goat implementations will not find them and will be confused about whether to name their classes with or without the Space prefix.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class identifiers consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution classes SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, Goat respectively so they match the problem statement and template Main, or (B) add small wrapper classes named Seal, Pig, Goat in the solution repository that extend/delegate to SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat (e.g., public class Seal extends SpaceSeal { public Seal(String n){ super(n); } }). Additionally, update the solution's README or the problem statement/template if the 'Space' prefix is intended, so students are explicitly informed of the naming choice.
